t_origin: t = frame_index / fps, frame 0 = first frame of the clip
convention: meters; origin = center dot; +x along the long axis toward the net at the top of the screen; +y = screen left (x then y counterclockwise on screen); z not observable (always 0)
scale_source: REAL METERS: rescaled x1.0873 from placeholder meters (python -m measure.rescale). Scale ESTIMATED from the in-game SHOT SPEED readouts of 4 ground goals (median 0.06418 m/px, spread (CV) 2.5%), ASSUMING the mph readout is in real units (measure/results/scale.json). Before: ICE-PLANE scale for puck motion: params.json rink_length = 60 m (PLACEHOLDER, unmeasured) / inner board length 914.00 px x (1 + k_board +0.00000); the board outline is at ice level within k_board = -0.00244 +- 0.00144, so board and ice scales agree. Puck positions are blob centroids reprojected to the ground (see track.json puck_parallax).
z: always 0: a top-down view cannot see height (a lifted puck also appears displaced toward the camera)
camera_correction: per-frame translation from the faceoff landmarks, undone before detection; u_px/v_px are reference-frame pixels, shift_u/shift_v the frame's measured shift

detector.gate_source: 2 x max speed cap 45 m/s (PLACEHOLDER) / 60 fps / 0.06565 m/px (PLACEHOLDER scale)

position_note: CSV x/y = ground points (ug_px, vg_px): blob centroids reprojected for the puck's height (puck_parallax)
